correctness.rationale: For each within-part matching pair uv, there are at least k vertices outside its part. An unmatched outside vertex yields a three-point difference expansion. Otherwise among the other k-1 pairs one pair is entirely outside and a four-point Garnir identity gives two cross-part matchings. The number of within-part pairs decreases in both cases, proving Pk(G)=Pk(K_n) for all k through nu. An elementary selected-vertices matching construction proves nu=min(floor(n/2),n-max part). The initiating source supplies and proves the characteristic-zero complete-graph two-row Specht dimension and graded duality; those facts are not claimed new. The packaged verifier independently checks 217 degrees on 58 multipartite profiles and 20 no-matching degrees modulo prime 1000003; these finite calculations corroborate but do not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The manuscript arXiv:2609.34260v2 gives full matching-difference dimensions for complete graphs, sufficiency of k-linkedness, a matching-complement sufficient condition and its complete multipartite corollary only when all parts have size two. It does not state the equality or Hilbert-series formula for arbitrary complete multipartite graphs. The new replacement induction proves the missing coverage, including all complete bipartite graphs in top matching degree where k-linkedness may fail. Targeted semantic and bibliographic searches found no dominating exact theorem; unresolved unindexed work remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible preprint may contain the same complete multipartite reduction under other algebraic terminology.
The examined manuscript may be revised after the inspected 2026-10-02 version; this comparison is version-specific.
Other characteristic regimes are not covered by the Hilbert-series assertion; the present theorem is stated in characteristic zero.

value.rationale: The initiating manuscript makes deciding k-saturation for graph families a structural research question. The theorem gives an exact all-size, all-degree answer for the canonical infinite class of complete multipartite graphs; it converts the graph connectivity obstruction into an if-and-only-if classification within this class, including families not covered by linkedness or matching-complement hypotheses, and determines a previously unspecified graph-algebra Hilbert series, with a sharp truncation at matching number. This is not ordinary matching enumeration and has concrete structural and algebraic content beyond a renaming exercise.
